text:
Noah: Hey folks - quick one. We have an adoption placement this week (foster-to-adopt). Placement order is in the social workers name for now and final adoption paperwork will be signed in ~10 weeks. Can I add the child during open enrollment as my dependent now, or do I need the final adoption decree?
Tess (People Ops): Congrats!! :tada: For foster placements that convert to adoption, carriers usually accept a placement/placement order plus a social worker letter as proof to enroll temporarily. Final adoption decree is ideal but not strictly required at enrollment if you submit the placement docs within the QLE window.
Noah: Awesome. Is there a recommended document checklist? Dont want to get bounced.
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/adoption-and-foster-placements - lists common docs (placement order, social worker letter, court notice, hospital docs if newborn, SSN application receipt).
Sam (Benefits): Checklist we use:
- Placement order or foster placement paperwork (PDF)
- Social worker letter on agency letterhead with placement date and expected custody status
- If available, hospital birth record or birth certificate (if already issued)
- If SSN not yet issued, SSN application receipt or signed affidavit
- Photo ID for employee and proof of relationship (placement docs suffice for foster/adopt)
Upload to People Ops > Manage Dependents and add a note "Noah - foster placement QLE".
Noah: If I enroll now with placement docs and the adoption finalizes later, will we need to re-submit anything?
Tess (People Ops): Good question. After enrollment well mark the dependent as "pending final paperwork." Once you upload the final adoption decree, well replace the provisional docs in the vendor file. This helps avoid gaps and ensures claims are paid correctly.
Legal (People Ops): From a legal side, carriers sometimes change the dependent's subscriber relationship when the final decree arrives (e.g., update name/DOB fields). Keep copies of any provider bills in case claims need appeals during the transition.
Noah: Payroll impact - will premiums start immediately? Im on salaried monthly payroll.
Sam (Benefits): Premiums: typically start the payroll period after Benefits processes the enrollment. If the effective date is backdated to the placement date (many carriers permit that if docs are timely), payroll will prorate accordingly and Payroll will issue any retro credits in the following pay cycle once Benefits confirms. If final adoption docs shift effective dates, we coordinate with Payroll for adjustments.
Noah: The social worker said SSN application will take a few weeks. Should I wait or upload the receipt now?
Tess (People Ops): Upload the SSN application receipt immediately. That plus the placement order should be enough to get provisional coverage. If the SSN arrives later, upload it and well update the record.
Noah: Any special notes about pediatricians billing since the child is technically still under the agency name?
Sam (Benefits): Providers often bill under the name on placement paperwork. If you get a denial, send the Explanation of Benefits (EOB) and bill/adjudication info to Benefits. We can open COB/appeal with the carrier. We can also produce an employer coverage confirmation letter to give to providers if helpful.
Noah: Uploaded placement order + social worker letter and left a note "Noah case AD-1099". Thanks!
Tess (People Ops): Case AD-1099 created. Well provisionally enroll the dependent with placement effective date and follow up if the carrier requires anything else. Expect confirmation email within 2 business days.
Noah: Appreciate it all - huge relief. :relieved:
Sam (Benefits): One more pointer: keep copies of any out-of-pocket receipts for up to 6 months in case retro coverage requires claim resubmission. Well also send you a checklist email with links to upload final decree when ready. :white_check_mark:
